## 5. Software

We provide two software solutions in relation to the current paper. An R package; nsgl, with relatively simple interface to our multinomial and logistic sparse group lasso regression routines. In addition; C++ template library; sg1, is provided. The template library gives access to the generic sparse group lasso routines. The R package relies on this library. The sg1 template library relies on several external libraries. We use the Armadillo C++ library [14] as our primary linear algebra engine. Armadillo is a C++ template library expression template techniques to optimize the performance of matrix expressions. Furthermore we utilize several Boost libraries [15]. Boost is a collection of free peer-reviewed C++ libraries; many of which are template libraries. For an introduction to these libraries see for example [16]. Use of multiple processors for cross validation and subsampling is supported through OpenMP [17]. sgl using

The nsg1 R package is available from CRAN. The sg1 library is available upon request.

## 5.1. Run-time performance

Table 3 lists run-times of the current multinomial sparse group lasso implementation for three real data examples. For comparison; the glmnet uses 5.2s, 8.3s and 137.0s, respectively; to fit the lasso for the three data sets in Table 3 The gImnet is a fast implementation of the coordinate descent algorithm for fitting generalized linear models with the lasso penalty or the elastic net penalty [10]. The gImnet cannot be used to fit models with group lasso or sparse group lasso penalty. path
